title: Glorious Knight
transcript: White forks the king and bishop, but actually after the king moves, the idea is not to take that bishop because otherwise after E2, there would be no way to prevent black from getting a new queen. We would have to pin the F3 pawn and at best this would be a draw. So actually after the rook check and after the king moves down, white collects the E3 pawn removing the last chance of black to promote [music] to a queen. Now the bishop is hanging and so is the knight and it doesn't seem like there's any way to save both of them. But black comes up with a brilliant idea. Bishop to E1, a move that creates a counter threat. If now the knight is taken, bishop to F2 would fork the king and knight and black would actually draw this game because a bishop and a pawn will be able to hold back one rook. But what black failed to realize is that white's plan is [music] not over. And after rook to G4 check, either the black king has to move away from the defense of F2 allowing white to win the knight or the king has to [music] move further down to F2. And now it seems like white can simply capture this knight defended by the king because after white takes, if the king captures on E3, we are going to be able to capture the bishop too and this is crushing. But actually after white takes the knight, black is not obligated to capture the other [music] knight and instead there is another brilliant plan that keeps the game going. King to E2. This not only keeps close contact with the knight, but it also frees up a red carpet for the black pawn. And if we try to step in front of the pawn defended by [music] the knight, black can just wait around and play for example bishop to H4 and now this becomes [music] a fork. There is no bishop hanging on E1 anymore, so we will have to at best get a draw for example like this. So is this it? Is black simply out of the woods? Well, not exactly. White plays to mysterious knight to F5. This simply allows black to push the F pawn and attack the white rook. And there is no way to keep the rook defending the F1 square. Or at least you would think that. But actually white has one last incredible ace up his sleeve. The majestic [music] rook to F1. This stops the pawn. And if the [music] king doesn't take the rook, we're now slowly going to drive the king away with our king and then bring the knight to the defense of the promotion, freeing up the rook. But of course the king can just capture that rook. But surprisingly, with only one knight left, white has knight to G3. Checkmate.
